characters.description: An absent adventurer whose allies are waiting to reunite with him. His earlier actions left him responsible for transformation zones and the people sheltered within his domains, and his friends remain apart while awaiting his return.
characters.name: Jason Asano

characters.description: Jason's independent shadow familiar and companion.
characters.name: Shade

characters.description: Jason's eye familiar and a source of magical advice who supports Jason's unusual magic.
characters.name: Gordon

characters.description: Jason's blood familiar and a powerful combat companion.
characters.name: Colin

characters.description: A magitech engineer, veteran adventurer and trusted member of Jason’s circle. She refuses to help intrude on her friends’ privacy.
characters.name: Farrah Hurin

characters.description: The protective leader of Team Biscuit and Sophie's partner. Humphrey has spent the years of Jason's absence advancing toward gold rank and preserving the team's cohesion, with the group intending to reunite fully once Jason returns.
characters.name: Humphrey Geller

characters.description: A Team Biscuit adventurer and Humphrey’s partner. She has operated separately during the group’s advancement but remains among those waiting for Jason’s return.
characters.name: Sophie Wexler

characters.description: An infiltrator and member of Jason’s returning team. During the years apart, she has taught at the adventurer school run by Rufus Remore’s family.
characters.name: Belinda Callahan

characters.description: Team Biscuit's healer and a dependable member of Jason's wider circle. During the team's separation, he watches over a younger adventurer's varied assignments so that the Adventure Society cannot take advantage of an inexperienced recruit.
characters.name: Neil Devone

characters.description: Team Biscuit’s ritual and dimensional-magic specialist with a strong academic focus.
characters.name: Clive Standish

characters.description: A storm mage who joined Team Biscuit during Jason's absence.
characters.name: Zara Noreen

characters.description: A veteran adventurer and close ally of Jason who has spent years on Earth. He supports the hidden Asano clan refuge while Jason remains away.
characters.name: Rufus Remore

characters.description: An Earth ally of Jason and a powerful member of the Asano clan’s wider circle.
characters.name: Taika

characters.description: A Healer priest and researcher working with Jason's allies. His long-term project seeks to remove severe magical corruption and develop a treatment for victims forced into vampirism.
characters.name: Carlos Quilido

characters.description: A trusted healer and mental-health specialist within Jason's circle.
characters.name: Arabelle Remore

characters.description: An adventurer from Jason's former Earth-era community.
characters.name: Cassandra Mercer

characters.description: Sophie's mother and a victim of imposed faith magic.
characters.name: Melody Jane

characters.description: A figure sought by Earth officials for information after the appearance of the new System interface.
characters.name: Boris Ket Lundi

characters.description: Time's prime avatar, who remains behind to guide Jason after the great astral being departs.
characters.name: Wraith

characters.description: The leader of a nine-person veteran mercenary team covertly observing the former Asano territory in France. He is weighing whether the Asano clan could offer lasting security to his team and their families.
characters.name: Gold-rank mercenary

characters.description: The leader of Brightheart City, which she maintained through the years without Jason's aura protection.
characters.name: Council Leader Loren

characters.description: A cosmic being who returns the unused value of Jason’s former resurrection agreement, allowing him to create a prime avatar.
characters.name: Death

characters.description: The son of Cassin Amuz, Gibson is the first patient to complete Carlos Quilido’s corruption-removal procedure. He survives the treatment and begins recovering.
characters.name: Gibson Amuz

characters.description: The leader of a group the Asano clan is considering accepting after its current job is complete.
characters.name: Nigel

characters.description: A highly sought communications and coordination specialist who works through the Adventure Society.
characters.name: Nick

characters.description: The god who embodies rulership. He gives Jason a means to hide his transcendent presence and counsels him about the political risks of returning to Earth.
characters.name: Dominion

characters.description: A diamond-ranker who challenges Jason after the Cloudflask passes beyond their control. Their encounter produces a wary arrangement for sharing guidance while avoiding a clash between exceptionally powerful figures.
characters.name: Cloudweaver

characters.description: An Adventure Society official chosen to handle the organization's dealings with Jason because he speaks candidly instead of showing excessive respect.
characters.name: Miguel Ladive

characters.description: One of the allies who gathers with Jason's wider circle in Outer Rhexion as the group prepares for its journey.
characters.name: Estella Warnock

characters.description: A gold-rank mercenary whose team survives and liberates a blood farm before returning to territory under Asano control.
characters.name: Nigel Thornton

characters.description: A politically experienced member of Jason's extended circle whom he asks to advise on his return to Earth. She presses him to define concrete objectives, gather reliable intelligence and recognize that restraint alone is not a complete diplomatic strategy.
characters.name: Danielle Geller

characters.description: An Earth official facing international pressure over the new System and the renewed activity in former Asano territory. She has an off-books observation team in Europe and must assess reports that Jason, his clan and a liberated blood farm are connected.
characters.name: Annabeth Tilden

characters.description: Segarado's gold-rank elven general and local defence commander. She organizes resistance after an unexpectedly large messenger force breaks the city's barrier, continuing to direct the battle even though her comparatively weak army expects to lose.
characters.name: Millicent Marx

characters.description: An astral king whose service has been penetrated by an undercover member of the Unorthodoxy.
characters.name: Vesta Carmis Zell

characters.description: Greenstone's Adventure Society director, preparing anxiously for Jason's formal return. Their prior conflict makes her fear retaliation, while a standing low-alert order and the city's political reception leave her responsible for managing his disruptive arrival.
characters.name: Elspeth Arella

characters.description: An experienced silver-rank operator from Earth who covertly manipulates rural protection rackets across low-magic regions. She exploits conflict between workers and aristocratic owners to fund the purchase of gold-rank monster cores.
characters.name: Earth refugee operator

characters.description: A senior astral king who opposes the unauthorized assault on Jason and confronts the four astral kings responsible for it.
characters.name: Council of Kings member

characters.description: A non-combatant from Greenstone who accepts a trial position as bartender and kitchen manager aboard Jason's cloud ship. The job offers travel and experience, but also requires discretion and an understanding that service around powerful adventurers carries unusual risks.
characters.name: Jamar

characters.description: A teenage Leonid with skill in magitech mechanics and a connection to Emmy's household.
characters.name: Young Leonid mechanic

characters.description: Jason's niece.
characters.name: Emmy

characters.description: Rufus Remore's diamond-rank grandfather. He draws Jason into the Burning Violet Guild's internal dispute as a diversion meant to distance Team Biscuit from his approaching confrontation with the Order.
characters.name: Roland Remore

characters.description: A diamond-ranker who explains the customary restraints on immortal power. He accepts Jason's System sanction as the large intervention permitted to a new immortal, but says the diamond-rank community will not protect him if he brings overwhelming force into routine mortal conflicts.
characters.name: Vandrick Maccaro

characters.description: An Earth expatriate, Cabal member and troll were-crocodile who joins the return group. Near gold rank, he hopes to gain access to Jason's network and magical knowledge.
characters.name: Daryl

characters.description: An Earth expatriate of Maori heritage who was transported to Palimastus while visiting a portal site and trained there without monster cores.
characters.name: Koa

characters.description: The royal identity resumed by the storm mage previously known publicly as Zara Noreen. She remains with Team Biscuit while preparing a gradual political campaign against indentured servitude in the Storm Kingdom, using domestic support rather than outside compulsion.
characters.name: Princess Zara Rimaros

characters.description: The official directing the fortified Australian dimensional-artifact site. She coordinates the multinational installation's response after sabotage and prepares for the unexpected arrival of Jason's representatives.
characters.name: Artifact-site director

characters.description: A Jakar pirate captain sent to Earth under a contract to remove Jason. Cautious about both the mission and his sponsors' incomplete account, he investigates Jason's cosmic connections while weighing the threat of a mutiny within his own gold-rank crew.
characters.name: Jota Withers

characters.description: The matriarch of a rival Japanese-origin Asano clan that hosts the pirate crew sent to remove Jason. She opposes Jason's side of the family.
characters.name: Asano Noriko

characters.description: Jota Withers's first officer and trusted second-in-command. She warns him that a rival is gathering support for mutiny, helping the captain assess whether their assignment against Jason has become more dangerous than its sponsors admitted.
characters.name: Natala

characters.description: A gold-rank Jakar pirate building support to replace Jota Withers as captain. He sees the contract against Jason as an opportunity to exploit any sign of weakness or failure in the existing command structure.
characters.name: Kriegel

characters.description: Lenora oversees security at Artifact City while its occupants withdraw and its defences are readied before Jason reaches the site.
characters.name: Lenora

characters.description: A young Leonid refugee and skilled magitech mechanic travelling with Jason's Earth-side representatives. Named for Jason's deceased friend, Gary is treated as his own person and joins Jason to help inspect and operate the newly captured dimension ship.
characters.name: Gary Sharpton

description.text: He Who Fights with Monsters 12 opens as Jason Asano survives a cosmic restoration that leaves him fundamentally changed, now the source of a new magical system suddenly available to people across countless worlds. Struggling to manage the scale of his own power and the obligations tied to it, Jason works to build a stable form he can use to move freely again, reconnect with old allies, and settle unfinished business in the territories and city that once depended on him. As he prepares to return to Earth, he must first navigate wary former allies, political suspicion from other powerful beings, and the practical challenge of appearing anything close to ordinary again.

recaps.ending:
Jason reaches Earth through the newly activated but still unstable bridge, backed by Team Biscuit, returning expatriates, researchers, clergy and a Storm Kingdom delegation. His plan to provoke a manageable pirate incursion damages trust with Annabeth Tilden and confirms that his political organization still lacks firm rules for consultation and authority.

At Artifact City, Jota Withers and Natala step aside from Kriegel's mutiny. Jason and Team Biscuit defeat the attacking gold-rank pirates, and Jason abandons the original plan to kill them. One pirate dies after apparently trying to purge Jason's afflictions, but the others are imprisoned in Jason's soul realm. Jason claims their dimension ship, brings Gary Sharpton into the effort to examine it and leaves Jota and Natala available for questioning.

Jason then departs to see Emmy. The pirate assault is over, but its Earth sponsors and the wider Jakar threat remain open. New Water still shelters Boko's survivors, the messenger conflict and vampire crisis continue, the inter-world bridge needs years to stabilize, and Jason's advisers must turn his immense personal power into a workable relationship with Earth.
recaps.in_short: After restoring the Cosmic Throne, Jason Asano becomes an immortal astral nexus and creates a prime avatar capable of leaving his domains. He reunites with Team Biscuit, survives an assassination that destroys Boko, shelters its people in New Water and forces a major messenger withdrawal. On the journey toward Earth, he uses the System against slavery and gathers stranded Earth expatriates. A new dimensional bridge carries his allies and a diplomatic expedition home. There, Jason admits that he deliberately enabled a limited Jakar pirate incursion to expose hostile Earth factions and create a common enemy. Team Biscuit defeats the mutinous pirates, and Jason chooses capture over execution. He ends the book holding their crew and dimension ship while the sponsors of the attack remain unidentified, then leaves the aftermath to his allies so he can reunite with his niece Emmy.

recaps.text: Previously: Jason Asano became separated from his allies after taking control of transformation zones and assuming responsibility for the people sheltered in his domains. His friends continued advancing toward gold rank and dispersed with the intention of reuniting when he returned. The Asano clan remained hidden on Earth, where Rufus Remore supported its survival amid vampire-held territory. Carlos Quilido pursued treatments for severe magical corruption and forced vampirism, while Team Biscuit and its wider circle carried on without Jason. Belinda Callahan taught at the Remore family's adventurer school, and Neil Devone watched over a younger recruit whose broad assignments left him without a permanent team. Jason departed again and remains absent. His allies await his return, but the consequences of his earlier actions have also drawn the attention of many others who want answers from him.

Jason survives restoring the Cosmic Throne, but his true self is now a universe and his mortal body is only an avatar. The restoration imprints him on the throne and creates a System interface for essence-capable people across the cosmos, provoking political upheaval, persecution and violence before he can return home. Wraith explains that he first needs a prime avatar and must rebuild the bridge between worlds.

Jason explores his inner universe and visits his grandmother, but his basic avatars cannot leave his territory. He reclaims reality-core power from vampires occupying the former Asano domain in France, destroying their city and arranging help for their blood-farm victims. After reopening the link to Brightheart City, he negotiates limits on his dominion and informs its leader about the sealed messenger world within his realm. Jason still lacks enough power for a prime avatar until Gordon suggests revisiting his former bargain with Death. Because resurrection is no longer possible for him, Death returns the unused reality material. Jason combines it with what he recovered and creates a prime avatar that can finally travel beyond his domains.

Jason uses his realm's control over pain and death to help Carlos Quilido remove corrupting magic from Gibson Amuz. Gibson survives, but the procedure still depends on Jason's domain and is not yet a general cure. Jason studies the abilities of his prime avatar while Rufus helps the Asano clan receive survivors from vampire blood farms.

After years confined to his territories, Jason crosses into Outer Rhexion. He can suppress much of his overwhelming presence, although his speech and physical existence remain difficult to disguise. He reunites with Zara Noreen, who confirms that she has become a full member of Team Biscuit, and learns that Clive's dimensional expertise will be needed for the route to Earth. Dominion gives Jason a means of concealing his transcendent nature but warns that his political position cannot remain ambiguous. Diamond ranker Cloudweaver then confronts him over the altered cloud flask. Their exchange establishes a cautious relationship in which high-rankers may guide Jason in mortal affairs while he offers insight into transcendence. By chapter 15, Team Biscuit and its allies have gathered and agreed to collect Earth expatriates before repairing the inter-world link.

Jason tests his new combat form in a mirage arena against a gold-rank prince. Although the prince dismembers the projected body, Jason regenerates, drains the prince's magical after-images and wins when the swordmaster yields. The display also alters the arena's projection system, giving Clive another mystery to investigate.

Farrah Hurin then confronts Jason about their bond. His transformation has stalled her advancement and is pushing her toward magical service as his Voice of the Will. Jason admits that part of his own subconscious is trying to impose that outcome. Inside his astral kingdom, he offers to sever the bond or replace it with an immortal arrangement that protects her autonomy and allows her to oppose his influence. Farrah accepts an alternative and survives the resulting advancement surge, although the exact status she chose is not established.

Recognizing the danger his power will pose on Earth, Jason recruits Danielle Geller as a political adviser. She requires clear objectives, intelligence and limits rather than vague intentions. With his cloud vessel upgraded, Jason's expedition leaves Yoresh on an indirect route that allows both preparation and reconnaissance.

The expedition diverts to Segarado when a large messenger force attacks the poorly defended city. Jason's party and the local army destroy the attackers without a Segarado military death. General Millicent Marx remains concerned that the assault had a specific hidden objective, while Jason's identity as the Heretic King alarms the surviving messenger leadership.

Elsewhere, an undercover Unorthodoxy voice exposes herself during debate over whether the messengers should avoid or attack Jason. On Earth, Rufus Remore invites Annabeth Tilden to become Jason's senior political adviser and tells her that Jason expects to return within a year. The travelling group continues through the Dragonlands, leaving quickly after Clive enters a restricted magical hall and Zara rejects a prince's coercive attempt to make her his wife.

Jason then reaches Greenstone in secret with Belinda Callahan and Estella Warnock. Before the public arrival, he revisits the abandoned waystation where he was tortured as an iron ranker. He acknowledges how the ordeal shaped his identity and recovery, while Greenstone's Adventure Society prepares nervously for the disruptive return of a far more powerful Jason.

Jason quietly helps Greenstone's surrounding communities before Team Biscuit receives an official welcome. Adventure Society director Elspeth Arella asks him to investigate a rural movement exploiting genuine worker grievances. Belinda and Estella trace its organizer to an experienced Earth refugee, whom Jason considers recruiting after vetting.

An armored assassin then impales Jason with a weapon that drains his astral kingdom. Jason evacuates most of Boko while Clive, Farrah and Belinda build a containment ritual, but his avatar explodes and devastates the city. A messenger army descends as the System declares the rise of the Hegemon. Jason manifests as a ghost-fire phoenix, destroys the attackers and reaches through their portals to kill the four voices directing the assault. The victory saves most civilians but kills hundreds or more during the evacuation and blast, and Jason is burdened by having deliberately killed roughly ten thousand indoctrinated messengers.

A senior astral king identifies Jason as an originator who combines several kinds of cosmic authority. Jason demands that messenger occupiers leave Palimustus and that their marked forces be freed. A much larger surrendered force subsequently enters his realm, where he also creates a refuge for Boko's displaced population.

The Adventure Society grants Jason the broad autonomy normally given to diamond rankers while retaining an expectation that he answer major crises. He names the refuge for Boko's people New Water and removes the former duke from authority there, asking the gods to help establish resident choice and governance without inherited titles. Jason also promises to take greater responsibility for Nick, who is his living creation and regards him as a father.

On Earth, an international delegation enters the restored Asano territory. Jason explains the transformation zones, the clan's vampire rescues and the danger his eventual return may create. After several days of examination, Annabeth Tilden provisionally accepts his offer to advise him, subject to further verification.

Jason's party reaches Vitesse and the Remore Academy. His quiet application to the Burning Violet Guild becomes entangled in a factional dispute over the Remore family's influence. Roland Remore admits that he deliberately drew Jason into the issue to keep Jason and Humphrey away from Roland's coming conflict with the Order. Jason refuses involvement, and Humphrey formally withdraws Team Biscuit from the guild.

Jason reconnects with Cassandra Mercer, who refuses immediate contact with Neil after he ended their relationship without consulting her. Team Biscuit then takes a Springclaw Gorilla contract to rebuild its tactics now that every member is gold rank and Jason has rejoined the active formation.

In Syrian, the group gathers stranded Earth expatriates. When noble houses use indenture laws to retain Earthling guards, Jason announces that he will withdraw System access from every jurisdiction maintaining slavery or equivalent servitude. Diamond ranker Vandrick Maccaro treats this as Jason's single major intervention as a new immortal but warns that other immortals will not support further interference in mortal disputes. Belinda abducts the negotiating nobles and places them in Sadi Andali's slave markets, forcing their families into rescue operations and helping secure the Earthlings' release.

The expedition leaves with dozens of returnees and continues its pickup route. At a mountain city, Storm Spire Drakes attack the skyport. Team Biscuit, Koa, Daryl, Nick and local adventurers coordinate through Jason's System tools, eliminate the silver-rank swarm and preserve the local gold-rank defenders' control of their own battle.

The last Earth returnees gather on a Storm Kingdom island containing infrastructure that can anchor a dimensional bridge. Zara Noreen resumes her royal identity as Princess Zara Rimaros and begins planning a gradual domestic campaign against indenture. Clive activates the bridge, although it will take about a decade to stabilize for routine travel. Jason's cloud ship follows it through the deep astral with the expatriates, Team Biscuit, researchers, clergy and a Storm Kingdom delegation.

On Earth, Jason offers sane vampires resettlement on a safely eclipsed world and prepares to destroy those beyond recovery. American officials warn him that several governments have invited Jakar pirates to eliminate him. Jason then admits that he used a cosmic favor to permit gold-rank outsiders into Earth, deliberately creating a manageable enemy that might unite local factions and demonstrate that he cannot be controlled. Annabeth Tilden condemns his failure to consult the advisers he recruited, and Jason accepts the need for a formal organization around his power.

Ahead of his arrival, Annabeth, Rufus Remore, Taika and a young Leonid specialist enter the fortified Australian standing-stone site and begin direct negotiations with its leadership.

Pirate captain Jota Withers discovers that his local sponsors have understated Jason's power and that Kriegel is organizing a mutiny. When Jason reaches Artifact City, Jota and Natala disclose the split and withdraw from the fight, while Kriegel leads twenty-three gold-rank pirates against Jason.

Jason initially fights alone, spreading darkness, shadow doubles, draining effects and aura suppression across the pirate force. Once the attackers pin him with a harpoon, Team Biscuit and Farrah enter the battle. Belinda pulls the pirates together, the team exploits Jason's accumulated afflictions and the mutineers collapse. Jason abandons the planned execution, deciding that the public victory has made his point and that he does not want to repeat the person he was when he left Earth.

The team captures the fleeing dimension ship. One pirate dies after apparently trying to remove Jason's afflictions, but the survivors enter imprisonment in his soul realm. Jason claims the ship from Earth authorities and recruits Gary Sharpton to help examine it. Jota and Natala remain available for questioning, while the attack's Earth sponsors are still unknown. Jason delegates the aftermath and leaves through Shade to reunite with Emmy.

characters.description: An astral king of gold rank who has come back to Earth in his prime avatar, in person rather than through avatars, to repair his relationships with family. He meets his sister Erika again in Saint Etienne, sees his niece and his late brother's family, and handles diplomacy with the Australian government at the same time. He accepts that Australia will take back the Standing Stones but asks for a public apology over the seizure of Asano Village, and then opens a portal to his own kingdom.
characters.name: Jason Asano

characters.description: Jason's older sister, who calls him her little brother. She lives in Saint Etienne with her husband Ian and their daughter Emmy. On a rooftop at her home she and Jason talk through the distance that grew between them after his previous stay on Earth, and he explains why he waited until he could come back in person.
characters.name: Erika

characters.description: Erika's husband and the father of Emmy Evans-Asano. He is part of the family in Saint Etienne that Jason comes back to Earth to reconnect with.
characters.name: Ian Evans-Asano

characters.description: Jason's niece, the daughter of Erika and her husband Ian. Jason meets her again as part of his return to Earth after years away, during the same visit in which he sees the rest of his family in Saint Etienne.
characters.name: Emmy Evans-Asano

characters.description: A former United Nations and network figure who now works for Jason as his chief political advisor for Earth. She supplies the list of conspirators behind the pirates who tried to kill Jason, a list that is said to include the Australian Prime Minister.
characters.name: Anna Tilden

characters.description: A rabbit-like humanoid who is also a sun, created by accident when Jason rewrote reality. Jason left him alone for about fifteen years and now apologises, promising to be present in his life. Nick is anxious but easy to love, and his powers work best in large groups. Jason's family greets him warmly, and Jason admits to Erika that he made Nick and then abandoned him.
characters.name: Nick

characters.description: Jason's father. When Jason admits to Erika that he created Nick and then stayed away from him for about fifteen years, Ken stands by his son.
characters.name: Ken Asano

characters.description: Jason's grandmother on his father's side and the matriarch of Clan Asano. She is able to change how old she appears, and she is with the rest of Jason's family when Nick meets them.
characters.name: Yumi Asano

characters.description: A friend of Jason's from the other world who is staying on the cloud ship. He trained Jason's nieces Hannah and Jace in aura control during Jason's absence, and he bakes cakes, some of them magical and some of those prone to exploding.
characters.name: Rufus Remore

characters.description: A researcher from Jason's circle who, together with a colleague, has spent close to twenty years reverse engineering a portal network. Jason wants a small new guild to serve as a testbed for that network once he returns to Palimustus.
characters.name: Clive

characters.description: A researcher who has worked alongside Clive for close to twenty years to reverse engineer a portal network. Jason hopes a small new guild can serve as a testbed for that network once he goes back to Palimustus.
characters.name: Lorelei

characters.description: A member of Jason's circle who is aboard the cloud ship with Rufus Remore and Gary while Jason reconnects with Nick and his family.
characters.name: Taika Williams

characters.description: Jason's shadow companion, who works as his personal portal system and assistant. Shade keeps track of events for him and is the one who reports that the disappearance of the Australian officials touring Jason's realm has been noticed.
characters.name: Shade

characters.description: Humphrey's mother, part of the group from Palimustus visiting Earth with Jason. She meets Anna Tilden and Erika at the barbecue on the cloud ship, and Jason asks her to explain the politics of Palimustus to Erika so that his sister understands why his relationship with Zara is complicated. She begins the account with a visit from Rufus Remore.
characters.name: Danielle Geller

characters.description: A princess of the Storm Kingdom. Her lady-in-waiting Zerine encourages her to go and see Jason. Jason tells Erika that his relationship with Zara is a complicated political matter, and he asks Danielle Geller to explain the politics of Palimustus to his sister for that reason.
characters.name: Zara

characters.description: One of Jason's teammates from the other world. She comes to the barbecue on the cloud ship together with Estella, where Jason's friends from both worlds mix.
characters.name: Belinda

characters.description: Belinda's wife. She comes with Belinda to the barbecue on the cloud ship, where Jason's friends from the other world and his family from Earth spend time together.
characters.name: Estella

characters.description: One of Jason's teammates from the other world, present at the barbecue on the cloud ship where his friends and his Earth family meet.
characters.name: Sophie Wexler

characters.description: The wife of Travis, one of Jason's friends from the other world. She comes with her husband to the barbecue in the lounge of the cloud ship, where Jason's teammates and his Earth family mix.
characters.name: Gabrielle

characters.description: An old messenger, an angelic type of being, who has lived on Earth for eons and hides at Cabal headquarters in what was the Democratic Republic of Congo. He says a dimensional bridge to Palimustus was put in place long ago and that Earth will have a true passage between worlds within about ten years. He deliberately keeps what is coming from Jason, fearing that Jason's risky solutions would endanger the bridge.
characters.name: Boris Ket Lundi

characters.description: A tall winged messenger whose history with Jason is painful. She talks with Boris Ket Lundi about whether she should go to Australia, where Jason is, and has not made up her mind.
characters.name: Tera Jun Casta

characters.description: A diamond-rank admiral in command of an enemy fleet, served by a staffer named Keeley. He notices that the gold-rank agents sent to Earth on his behalf have stopped reporting, suspects that someone is playing him, and orders that all available information on Earth be gathered.
characters.name: Jakar

characters.description: A gold-rank vampire leader. The vampires under her may hold weapons capable of wiping out cities, which is why Jason is delaying decisions. He expects her to bargain and is considering offering her and other vampires exile on a distant planet in his universe.
characters.name: Elizabeth

characters.description: A priest travelling on Jason's cloud ship. He is one of the healers on hand after the Melbourne bunker operation, when Jason's team gathers with the rescued mercenaries and other survivors.
characters.name: Carlos Quilido

characters.description: A servant of Jason's with blood-red eyes, a blood clone made of a swarm of leeches. In the bunker where vampires are loading a nuclear weapon, he introduces himself to the vampire lord Loudon, who attacks him, and he comes apart into leeches and bites back.
characters.name: Colin

characters.description: The healer of Jason's team from the other world. After the bunker operation in Melbourne he treats the rescued mercenaries and other survivors.
characters.name: Neil Devone

characters.description: Danielle Geller's son and a member of Jason's team. During the hunt for the blood oak in Melbourne he leads in expedition mode and can field up to a hundred gold-rank warriors summoned from dragon teeth.
characters.name: Humphrey Geller

characters.description: A healer from the other world who leads a team of her own, including a tracker named Callum. She takes part in the Melbourne operation in which four gold teams hunt and kill the blood oak.
characters.name: Arabelle Remore

characters.description: A friend of Jason's from the other world who came to the barbecue with his wife Gabrielle. After the bunker raid he identifies the recovered device as a nuclear weapon with faded magical enhancements and renders its material inert. Jason then asks him and Clive to study the sealed lab the teams discover.
characters.name: Travis

characters.description: A member of Clan Asano who was once a cardinal of the Engineers of Ascension, known as Mrs South, and who came back from the dead as an energy vampire, a different creature from ordinary vampires and unaffected by magical sunlight. Years ago Jason's grandmother removed her from the network. Since then she has carried out hidden research, and no one on Earth knows more about how Magitek interacts with living bodies, which is why she is brought to the Melbourne lab.
characters.name: Audrey Blaine

characters.description: The head of the multinational body that runs a former village the Australian government has declared a neutral territory, set aside for the refugee handover and for future summits.
characters.name: Lenora Coleman

characters.description: A silver-rank officer of the Australian intelligence service who is assigned to Jason as a liaison. She was trained in the aura-control methods developed by Jason's friends from the other world.
characters.name: Natalie Park

characters.description: Earth's first Leonid to be born naturally, named after an earlier Gary who was a Leonid friend of Jason's party. He is keenly aware of how powerful Jason is and asks why people treat him as special. Jason shows him a scene of the first Gary and promises to give him an answer.
characters.name: Gary

characters.description: A Celestine and the mother of Sophie Wexler, and the longest-serving resident of Jason's realm. She has recovered after surgery removed a substance that had been controlling her mind. She walks the tree city of Arbor with Jason, who tells her the city has its own soul and avatar and that forests across the planet are growing pods that will one day produce messengers.
characters.name: Melody Jane

characters.description: The United States Secretary of State and a friend of Anna Tilden. She and Anna discuss how to share Jason's full explanation of the wider cosmos without political fallout, and they lean toward forming a new secret group of key people.
characters.name: Claire

characters.description: A member of Jason's group from Palimustus and an expert on Earth's magical grid. At the manifestation in Pakistan she studies the site and concludes that it is a monster wave that has been artificially accelerated.
characters.name: Farrah Hurin

characters.description: A network director based in Zermatt at a time when the network is divided into four factions. She approves an intervention on the grid and, when an analyst reports tampering that feeds magic into the Pakistan manifestation, chooses not to warn the group fighting there. She is secretly behind the grid sabotage.
characters.name: Marie Finnegan

characters.description: A swordsman of the Remore family who fights beside Rufus Remore against the monsters pouring out at the Pakistan manifestation.
characters.name: Gabriel Remore

characters.description: One of Jason's familiars. Along with the familiars Stash and Shimmer, he joins the fighting at the gold-rank manifestation in Pakistan while Farrah Hurin works to shut down the points interfering with the grid.
characters.name: Gordon

characters.description: A ritualist from Earth who led the Earth researchers in the original grid work group. He resented Farrah Hurin's authority, argued against shelving dangerous research, and vanished after the network split. He is treated as the leading suspect behind the artificial transformation zones. Anna knew him from the Australian network.
characters.name: Simon McKean

characters.description: Emmy's boyfriend, a swordsman trained by Rufus Remore who has reached upper silver and is close to gold. He is nervous about meeting Jason, who has watched him grow up from afar. Jason sits down with him and gives him the blessing Vincent has been waiting for before he proposes to Emmy.
characters.name: Vincent Baudrillard

characters.description: A member of Clan Asano from a Japanese family who has travelled with Jason. At the clan's beach outing he is in love with his best friend Akari Asano but has never told her.
characters.name: Itsuki

characters.description: A member of Clan Asano from its network branch and the best friend of Itsuki, who has quietly been in love with her. She is among the clan members at Jason's beach outing.
characters.name: Akari Asano

characters.description: The prime vessel of the Reaper. He has served Clan Asano as an obstetrician, helping reincarnated souls into new lives. Jason thanks him for that work, and Velius tells him he will be leaving Earth before long.
characters.name: Velius

characters.description: A soul trapped inside a degraded blood clone, kept as a slave by the vampire Elizabeth, with explosive powers. He was the network agent who broke Jason's ties with the network. He escapes from the network's Reality Core Depository with Elizabeth and Marie Finnegan.
characters.name: Jack Gerling

characters.description: A gold-rank portal user who opens the portal that lets Jack Gerling, Elizabeth and Marie Finnegan get away from the network's Reality Core Depository in the Alps.
characters.name: Remy

characters.description: A messenger who looks after the messengers within Clan Asano and is a friend of Tera Jun Casta. According to Boris Ket Lundi, when Tera's faith in the astral kings turned to fury, it was Jali who helped her join the unorthodoxy.
characters.name: Jali Corrik Fen

characters.description: The director of the Geneva branch of the network. Spanish drone footage shows her apparently in command of Geneva and Zurich branch staff at a hidden cave in the Alps, although both branches were believed to be inactive and are suspected of having made a deal with the vampires.
characters.name: Geneva Andros

characters.description: A Swiss gold ranker who fights with lightning. She and another Swiss gold ranker, Amstutz, meet the Geneva branch director on a flying bus at the hidden Alpine site as Jason's cloud ship approaches.
characters.name: Bussinger

characters.description: Shade's brother, a being who hates change and longs for a return to a blank state. He helped Shade's earlier summoner imprison Shade in the astral space where Shade first met Jason. Shade expects Umber to come back and cause trouble.
characters.name: Umber

characters.description: A UN Under-Secretary-General and silver anchor who took over the role Anna Tilden once held. She has a cat familiar named Gumboot. Jason's briefing and a tour of his universe convinced her that he is close to a god, and she now treats him like a natural disaster. She sees the collusion between the Swiss network branches and the vampires as her biggest problem. Her nephew Tim works as her assistant.
characters.name: Holly

characters.description: A vampire leader and an old friend of Jason's, whose vampires depend on the sanctuary city Jason provides. He demands that Elizabeth be handed to the vampires for justice. Jason refuses and keeps her in his custody for life, and Craig agrees to keep his vampires in check, but he leaves coldly and now deals with Jason as a ruler, not a friend.
characters.name: Craig Vermillion

characters.description: A gold-rank team leader allied with Jason's clan. He is hurt by a wounding affliction during a raid on a site Elizabeth supplied, and Neil treats him. He reports that Jack Gerling felt tainted with undeath, and Jason asks him for the whole story.
characters.name: Nigel Thornton

characters.description: A network defender for a small cathedral city in Wales who has only just reached silver rank, with gun, trap and skirmish essences, and who grew up admiring footage of Jason. A misreported manifestation throws iron lions at her, while vampires attack her team and cut off communications. She fights on until she collapses, and Jason arrives, ends the lions and tells her she did well.
characters.name: Delia

characters.description: She serves as the leading representative of the cosmic entity that rules over time. Once Jason's astral kingdom is complete, she visits him at its space station.
characters.name: Wraith

characters.description: A friend of Jason's who was the prime vessel of the world phoenix and has since become a transcendent. Boris believed she went beyond her mandate in her dealings with Jason, and she once talked Wraith out of killing him. She arrives at Jason's kingdom in a new avatar aboard a burning ship shaped like a phoenix, apologises for keeping secrets, and confirms a warning she cannot act on herself. She tells Jason to reach diamond rank before others learn who repaired the cosmic throne.
characters.name: Dawn

characters.description: A messenger astral king, regarded as the nearest thing to a single leader of the Council of Kings, though Jason considers him an outlier. Messengers he surrendered are held on a prison planet in Jason's kingdom. He approaches Thalia Mercer wanting to meet her transformed son Thadwick, then sends an avatar to Jason's universe, where he comments on the two messengers Jason freed.
characters.name: Jamis

characters.description: A gold ranker with an onslaught essence and the mother of Cassandra and Thadwick. While she watches her daughter from a distance, the messenger king Jamis confronts her, asks to meet her transformed son, and warns her that her broker is betraying her.
characters.name: Thalia Mercer

characters.description: Thalia Mercer's son, who has been transformed. The messenger king Jamis wants to meet him and says that his own people are also hunting Thadwick because of something he holds.
characters.name: Thadwick

characters.description: A general who arrives to command the offensive of the EDJI, a coalition of forty-seven nations whose participation was driven by human augmentation and the Quilido procedure. He wants to question Jason about the threat Jason keeps hinting at.
characters.name: Michael Mills

characters.description: A goddess of Palimustus. Jason names her, together with Purity and Disguise, among the gods he sees getting out of line, and he expects a coming clash between mortals and these gods, who can be pushed against their own rules but cannot be fought head-on.
characters.name: Knowledge

characters.description: One of the strongest vampire lords still alive, working with Simon McKean. She watches with him from a darkened monitor room as Jason breaks into McKean's castle in France.
characters.name: Magdalene

recaps.ending: Jason has killed Simon McKean and ended the vampires' mass revival, but he cannot stop the invasion Knowledge has spent five hundred years arranging, since an unfinished bridge would destroy both worlds. He leaves Earth to complete it. Nick, Erika, Ken, Emmy and the clan stay on Earth, where Anna Tilden and Michael Mills's EDJI prepare to defend the Outback Australia aperture against an expected magitek nuclear strike, and Clive and Emmy work on delaying measures. Farrah Hurin stays to support Jason's astral kingdom. Boris Ket Lundi leads the Cabal openly as the messengers withdraw. Jason surrenders his team at the island now called Ascension's Gate. Knowledge appears in person and tears the divine essence from her priestess Gabrielle, who is released with the others but needs a replacement essence. Diamond rankers led by Roland Remore and the Mirror King Victor Volare have struck a deal letting Knowledge proceed. Zara departs with the Storm Kingdom party. An envoy of the world phoenix, acting on Dawn's warning, shelters Jason's team in her ship. Shade's brother Umber has made Thadwick a leader in the Order of the Reaper, and Knowledge has set Thadwick to hunt Jason. Jason vows to kill Knowledge and enters the anchor ritual alone, to be bound to his prime avatar and sent somewhere that is not quite a universe. Open threads: his imprisonment, Knowledge's holy war, Jamis and the Council of Kings, the Bahraini leaders, surviving vampires, and the troubled marriages of Itsuki and Akari and of Travis and Gabrielle.
recaps.in_short: Jason Asano returns to Earth in person to mend family ties and deal with its governments, and is drawn into a widening war with vampires and rogue network factions. He kills a blood oak in Melbourne, stops an artificial monster wave in Pakistan, and exposes a reality-core farming scheme run by Marie Finnegan, the vampire queen Elizabeth and the ritualist Simon McKean. McKean abandons Elizabeth and Marie, who are then captured, and turns parasites and coordinated blood oaks against the world. Wraith and Dawn warn Jason of an unwinnable event he must hide even from his prime avatar. Two years later a 47-nation offensive stalls when slain vampires revive through a giant bloodroot vine fed by Jason's own bridge. Jason confronts McKean alone, turns the vine's link against him with his cosmic aura, and kills Jack Gerling and McKean. He then reveals that the goddess Knowledge has planned an invasion of Earth for five centuries and that he must finish the bridge regardless. He surrenders his team at Ascension's Gate, watches Knowledge strip her priestess Gabrielle's essence, and enters a ritual that will imprison him outside any ordinary universe.

recaps.text:
So far this book: Jason Asano comes back to Earth in person. In Saint Etienne he reconciles with his sister Erika and meets his niece Emmy, as well as Amy, widow of his late brother Kaito, and her daughters. Australian officials weigh his forces, and Anna Tilden's list of conspirators behind the pirates who tried to kill him includes the Prime Minister. Jason accepts Australia reclaiming the Standing Stones but asks for a public apology over the seizure of Asano Village. He apologises to Nick, the rabbit-like sun he made by accident and then left for fifteen years, and plans a small guild to test a portal network. A Chinese gold ranker who follows an open portal finds himself in Jason's personal universe, where Jason controls everything but souls, and Jason hints at a relic that could purge monster-core residue.

Out of Jason's sight, the old messenger Boris Ket Lundi says a bridge to Palimustus was laid long ago and will open within a decade; he keeps the coming danger from Jason. An enemy admiral, Jakar, senses that his agents on Earth have gone quiet.

Jason and the Storm Kingdom princess Zara grow close and kiss. He explains that he is delaying decisions because Elizabeth's vampires may hold weapons that can destroy cities. That proves true when the Prime Minister secretly sends Russian mercenaries after a vampire-held nuclear weapon in a Melbourne bunker, where a gold-rank blood oak has already caught one team. Jason rescues the survivors, freeing one captured team from the vampire curse entirely. His blood clone Colin consumes a vampire lord, four gold teams kill the blood oak, Travis renders the bomb inert, and a sealed lab is found.

So far this book: The Melbourne lab holds both magical and technological equipment. Jason brings in Audrey Blaine, a former Engineers of Ascension cardinal who came back as an energy vampire and knows Magitek biology better than anyone. Anna urges him to avoid new spectacles and to present himself as a humanitarian superhero, and she has assembled a think tank of experts. Australia turns a former village into a neutral territory under Lenora Coleman for the refugee handover. Boris tells Jason that the messengers' presence will be exposed eventually and that the Cabal wants to act publicly once before leaving.

Governments and factions confirm that more blood oaks exist, and the plan for a first strike against the vampires collapses; negotiating with Elizabeth is the fallback. Natalie Park becomes Jason's intelligence liaison. In his kingdom Jason walks the tree city of Arbor with Sophie's recovered mother, Melody Jane, and tells Gary, Earth's first natural-born Leonid, that he carries the reincarnated soul of Jason's late friend, though he is his own person.

A gold-rank manifestation appears on the Indus in Pakistan. Danielle Geller commands a large gold-rank force, while network director Marie Finnegan, who is secretly behind the grid sabotage, chooses not to warn them. Farrah Hurin finds an artificially accelerated monster wave, and Jason holds the rift shut at great cost while the teams fight; Rufus wipes out hundreds of monsters. Elizabeth and Marie are revealed as partners trying to create transformation zones for reality cores. Farrah recognises her own work in the sabotage and, with Nick's help, shuts down the interference points. Afterwards Claire, the US Secretary of State, sets out to befriend Jason, and Shade reveals his ancient nature to Anna.

So far this book: Anna sees how Jason's anger affects the land around him and leaves. Farrah tells her that the network man who imprisoned her, Adrien Barbou, was left to her judgement and implies he is dead. She warns that the elites of Palimustus will reshape Earth if its own powers do not police themselves. Her analysis shows that someone is deliberately creating transformation zones to harvest reality cores, probably in vampire-held Europe. Zara coaches Jason to show restraint and steady authority in public. At a multinational briefing the prime suspect becomes Simon McKean, a gifted Earth ritualist who opposed shelving dangerous research and vanished after the network split, and a young transformation-zone site is found in the Pyrenees.

Jason gives Emmy's boyfriend Vincent his blessing and takes his clan to a beach. He then asks the embittered messenger Tera Jun Casta to help rehabilitate the messengers surrendered by Jamis, who are held on a prison planet in his kingdom, and she chooses a home in a red-rock canyon. Meanwhile Elizabeth, Marie Finnegan and Elizabeth's blood-clone slave Jack Gerling flee the network's Alpine Reality Core Depository through a portal opened by Remy.

Spanish drone footage reveals a hidden Alpine cave, and Jason goes knowing it could be a trap. The Geneva branch finds seven containers of cores empty. Jason arrives on his cloud ship in battle form and takes on eight gold rankers. His afflictions and the spell Punition leave six of them close to death. One, Bussinger, burns off the afflictions with her own lightning and is spared.

So far this book: Bussinger, who has never killed anyone, did not know what the facility was for. Jason explains that removing enough reality cores would restart transformation zones and could eventually destroy the solar system. Remy names Marie Finnegan. Belinda opens the vault, which is confirmed to have held cores, and Farrah convinces Jason to leave the questioning to Anna and local authorities. In Slovakia, Carlos Quilido examines Bussinger with a ritual after Jason refuses to force her and she consents. Her lightning is slowly cleansing monster-core residue from her soul, and she agrees to research the problem with Carlos for years. Shade tells Jason he was born a shadow of the Reaper and warns that his brother Umber, who hates change, will return.

The investigation finds that Marie and Elizabeth worked with McKean from a roving submarine. On board, McKean has left a farewell video: he has destroyed his research, abandoned both women for other vampire lords, and left a project behind. When it is opened, a tentacle pierces Gerling and Elizabeth's link to him is taken over. On a UN jet, a silver-rank parasite bursts out of Holly's nephew Tim and kills him. Jason traps it and concludes that many such parasites may be hidden near important people. Zara's people capture Elizabeth and Marie after they come ashore in a storm. Jason agrees to let Earth's forces lead, while warning he will leave with his people if Earth's rule becomes intolerable. In his vampire city he offers Marie exile and Elizabeth a choice between cooperation and death, asking only that Gerling's soul be freed.

So far this book: Jason expects a new vampire war. McKean and other vampire lords now control the living weapons Elizabeth seeded across the world and intend to use them. Craig Vermillion demands Elizabeth for vampire justice. Jason refuses, and their friendship cools into the relationship of a ruler and his subject. Jason tells Anna he wants to give humans a way into magic without essences, done ethically. Gerling, now independent of Elizabeth and tainted with undeath, kills his own people to avoid capture. Elizabeth helps Jason's healers study the parasites and offers to build a ritual to detect the blood oaks, which are now acting in coordination. Holly, grieving, loses her UN post.

Vampires begin hitting lightly defended places. In Wales, Jason saves Delia, a newly silver defender, purges the vampire taint from her teammates, and learns the attackers were ordered to turn essence users against their town.

Wraith, vessel of the astral being of time, warns Jason that a coming event cannot be won and that repeated attempts using the link between worlds could cause a paradox destroying at least one universe. Dawn, now a transcendent, confirms it, tells him to keep it from his friends and his prime avatar until just before it starts, and urges him to reach diamond rank. Jason begins hearing prayers and realises he has become a kind of god. His prime avatar now has memories left out and seems colder. After a parasite kills three people on live television, Jason offers Earth open access to his magic and magitek for a decade on his terms, with an undisclosed Plan B, and helps save Nigel Thornton's team from nine vampire lords in Seoul.

So far this book: Two years later, the renewed vampire war is being held in Europe by enhanced human forces with magitek weapons. Carlos Quilido can now cure lesser vampirism without killing the host. Bahrain's government and ruling family have disappeared, and Venice is covered by glowing butterflies that form an eye visible from space. Jason confides to Anna that the Bahraini leaders are alive and farming on a prison planet, and the deaths in Bahrain weigh on him. Anna offers the United States access to them in exchange for recognising Clan Asano's sovereignty.

Jason works to stay human by spending time with family. Emmy will not fight monsters, and he predicts she will become Earth's first archwizard. Nick and the rest of the team keep advancing through gold, and thousands of cured former vampires live in Slovakian barracks under Arabelle Remore's care.

Farrah reports that McKean is allied with the vampires, that Gerling serves him and returns after death, and that a former network contact has offered McKean's location, presumed to be a trap at a castle in France. The messenger king Jamis approaches Thalia Mercer about her transformed son Thadwick and then visits Jason. He warns that Jason's prime avatar could be trapped, sealing his kingdom, and threatens to expose the hidden unorthodox messengers unless Jason shares the treatment Carlos developed for the vampires' weakness to sunlight. Jason gives it to him on a crystal. General Michael Mills arrives to lead the offensive of the 47-nation EDJI. Jason tells him McKean is his responsibility, that an army will come across the bridge, and that he himself will be taken from Earth before that war.

So far this book: In Jason's Cloud Palace, Mills approves a plan in which Jason confronts McKean loudly and alone while Clive, Belinda, Farrah, Sophie and Belinda's wife Estella slip in to find whatever McKean has prepared. Jason has a backup avatar built from vampire lords' core energy, so his body can be killed but not trapped. It is also revealed that Nick was made with soul engineering, a god-level magic. Akari Asano learns her husband Itsuki moved out weeks ago. Jason and Zara accept that they will part when they return to Palimustus, and Jason predicts trouble with the gods Purity, Disguise and Knowledge. His father Ken urges him to show compassion rather than godlike distance, and Jason says McKean is only a warm-up for worse enemies.

Craig says his vampires will stay on Earth. Jali tells Jason that refusing the messengers' choice to fight would mean they were never free, and Tera leads the clan's messengers. The offensive begins at midday. Belgrade is bombarded, including by Zara's hurricane, but slain vampires, ghouls and blood oaks rise again across Europe, and the allied forces fall back. In Multan, a life-drain spell is found to stop the revival. Farrah's detector shows thick red lines across the continent: a single enormous bloodroot vine that McKean has altered to bind vampire souls and rebuild their bodies, hidden in the grid and kept clear of clan territory. Its power comes from beyond Earth, probably a stabilised breach to the astral. Mills clears Jason to go in.

So far this book: Jason marches on McKean's castle in France with Shade, Gordon and Colin, while Humphrey destroys a target in Liechtenstein. McKean and the vampire lord Magdalene watch as he breaks in. McKean throws the lesser vampires at Jason to test him, saying he will prove Jason can be fought. Colin kills the vampires sent after him and withers the vines, and Jason wipes out the horde with blood magic and a transcendent rain of light. The infiltration team finds only research on grafting blood oaks.

In a steel dome full of roots, Jason faces Gerling, now a true undead full of cosmic power. Jason apologises to him and offers McKean talks, but McKean orders the kill. Jason rots Gerling's body away before the dome implodes. Clive recognises the system McKean is drawing on as the dimensional bridge he and Jason built, which cannot be shut down without tearing Earth's dimensional membrane. McKean betrays Magdalene by sending her reserve lords against the infiltrators, and Farrah kills them. Belinda proposes stopping the bridge's refinement of raw astral magic so that raw chaos poisons the vine. The only part that can be controlled is Jason himself.

Gerling rises again and vines pierce Jason, who lets them. Using the link, he channels his own cosmic power: the Hegemon rises, his aura tears the castle out of the ground, and his avatar burns into a black, starlit bird of fire. Vampire regeneration fails worldwide and revived vampires explode. Jason kills Gerling with a touch. McKean flees, sets off a monster wave, and is destroyed by the cloud ship's beam, predicting that humanity will one day turn on Jason.

So far this book: Clone bodies of McKean die as they grow, and Colin devours the whole vine. A week later the main fighting is over. Jason tells Anna that the goddess Knowledge has prepared an invasion of Earth for five hundred years and that he is part of her plan; stopping it would mean destroying the bridge and Earth with it, so he must return to Palimustus and complete the bridge. He tests Gabrielle, Travis's wife and a priestess of Knowledge, who holds to her faith. Before his assembled allies he explains the history: the cosmic throne was broken, the Builder created the twin worlds, Knowledge persuaded Purity to fade and helped Disguise take his place, the Network Founder's familiar became Mr North, and Jason himself was steered into the role he played. Knowledge must wage a holy war on Jason's domains to cross. When about a third of Knowledge's clergy are found to be spies, Jason spares them at Gabrielle's request.

Allies choose where to go. Nick stays on Earth, Zara's delegation returns to Palimustus, and Natalie, now married to Miguel with a newborn daughter, plans to move there. Yumi and Farrah steady Jason. He tells the EDJI that the bridge ends in Outback Australia and on a Storm Kingdom island seized by the Church of Knowledge, that a magitek nuclear strike is expected, and that the unfinished bridge would ruin both worlds within months; Knowledge wants to become Earth's only god, and he refuses that role himself. At a farewell festival Zara explains that marrying Jason would inflame the island dispute. Thadwick delivers the purity relic and is set to hunt Jason. Emmy insists on fighting, the Remores say goodbye to Rufus, and Farrah stays to guard Jason's kingdom as he prepares to leave Earth.

description.text: He Who Fights with Monsters 2 continues Jason Asano's efforts to help newcomers Sophie and Belinda escape exploitation in the city of Greenstone, offering Sophie protection and the resources to become an adventurer in her own right. As Sophie builds a new set of magical abilities and gains rank, Jason navigates political fallout from a disastrous expedition, an increasingly hostile magic society official, and a personal relationship that unravels under social pressure. Meanwhile, evidence mounts that survivors of the expedition were secretly altered by a hostile group, a threat that comes into sharp focus when a hidden, dangerous construct is found controlling one of the missing adventurers.

recaps.ending: Jason's six-person team settles into his soulbound Cloudflask houseboat and begins intensive training with its completed abilities and new familiars. Sophie and Belinda have both reached Iron rank, although Sophie's indenture and the threats from Lamprey and Cole remain unresolved. Jason holds the genuine Scythe of the Reaper and a Reaper token, but has not committed to the covert Order and still does not know how to use the World Phoenix token to reach Earth. The Builder crisis overtakes these gains. Dorgan's shipping evidence leads a mixed-rank strike force to a cult island, confirming Church of Purity involvement, constructs, and an extensive portal network. The cult withdraws while keeping Thadwick alive. Rufus recognizes Farrah's killer, exhausts himself using Kingdom of Eclipse against it, and collapses surrounded by enemies. The killer survives badly wounded, and Rufus's immediate fate is unresolved when chapter 76 ends.
recaps.in_short: Jason secures Sophie's indenture before Lamprey can claim it, helps her become an Iron-rank adventurer, and forms a team with Sophie, Humphrey, Clive, Neil, and eventually Belinda. Their investigation reveals that altered expedition survivors carry starseeds serving the Builder, whose followers steal astral spaces with covert Church of Purity support. During Emir's contest in Fallen Echoes, Jason's allies survive monsters, hostile entrants, and the Order of the Reaper's trials. Jason uncovers the Order's continuing secret network, wins its genuine scythe, and gains new familiar powers. Sophie and Belinda complete their advancement, and the team moves into Jason's Cloudflask houseboat. Dorgan then locates a cult island. A strike force attacks, but the cult escapes through portals with Thadwick still captive. Rufus finds Farrah's killer and wounds it with Kingdom of Eclipse, then collapses exhausted and surrounded as the book ends.

recaps.text: Previously: Jason Asano arrived in this world as an outworlder and became an Iron-rank adventurer in Greenstone. Rufus Remore, Gary, and Farrah became his mentors and allies, while Humphrey Geller and Clive Standish joined his growing circle. Jason also became involved in protecting Sophie Wexler and Belinda from the people seeking to control them. The conflict led to unresolved hostility from Magic Society director Lucian Lamprey, Adventure Society director Elspeth Arella, and Cole Silva. An expedition into an astral space ended in disaster. Farrah was killed, many other adventurers died, and the surviving force returned with evidence of an organized enemy using unusual magic and constructs. Rufus and Gary want to identify those responsible, while Jason must decide how best to protect Sophie without replacing one form of coercion with another. He also remains separated from his family on Earth and seeks a possible path between worlds.

So far this book: Jason offers Sophie and Belinda several ways out of Greenstone's criminal and political pressures. They choose a six-month indenture arrangement that can lead Sophie into the Adventure Society. Jason forces Arella to allow a fair hearing, and the Society claims Sophie's contract before Lamprey can take it. Sophie remains tracked and legally bound to Jason, but she and Belinda are housed safely in Emir's Cloud Palace. As the damaged expedition returns, Jason, Rufus, and Gary put their hunt for Farrah's killers on hold until the recovered evidence can be examined. With advice from Emir, Rufus, and Clive, Sophie adds Wind and Balance to her Swift Essence, creating the Mystic confluence. She reaches Iron rank with initial abilities that provide a ranged wind attack, meditative recovery, and protection against disruptive, dimensional, and astral effects. Jason makes clear that the powers are hers even after the contract ends, and Sophie begins to believe that his aim is lasting independence rather than ownership.

Sophie expands her movement and protective abilities, then starts practical monster training. Meanwhile, five expedition survivors show mismatched auras, changed personalities, and resistance to examination. They disappear before officials can secure them, and Anisa is revealed to the reader as a Purity priestess secretly coordinating with the hidden operation. Cassandra identifies her brother Thadwick as one of the five and briefly begins a relationship with Jason. The official inquiry demotes Jason to one Adventure Society star, after which Cassandra ends the relationship under Mercer family pressure. Jason refuses an offer from the Goddess of Knowledge to trade his faith for Farrah's killers, despite the temptation. Clive finds evidence that similar astral incidents have occurred elsewhere, while Rufus begins tracing specialized supplies through Greenstone and Hornus. Sophie and Jason acknowledge that their earlier approach to training had become controlling and restart as partners. The altered survivors are recovered in Hornus, leaving Greenstone with a chance to determine what has happened to them.

Sophie kills her first monsters alone and commits to an adventurer's path. Clive and Belinda upgrade a Geller mirage chamber to reconstruct the expedition evidence, while Rufus recruits Dorgan to investigate smuggling. A Purity cleansing ritual exposes a metal-wire construct threaded through an altered survivor, but destroying it kills the host. A second examination identifies the implant as a starseed, a transcendent device that replaces its host and can become impossible to remove. The remaining four seeded survivors escape custody. Clive's simulation shows that the expedition enemy was trying to sever an astral space from the world, and he identifies the Builder as the great astral being behind the operation. Its followers steal astral spaces to assemble a world in the deep astral, making the Greenstone incident part of a much wider threat. The group agrees to verify and distribute the discovery through trusted institutions while searching for the escaped hosts.

Emir reveals a nearby astral space accessible only to Iron-rank adventurers and urges Jason to build a balanced team for the coming contest. Jason recruits Neil Davone, an elven healer whose willingness to challenge his former church matters as much as his support powers. Humphrey becomes the team's central attacker, backed by Neil's shields and recovery, Clive's prepared magic, Sophie's interception, and Jason's disruptive afflictions. Gary and the Magic Society trace enemy constructs to imported clockwork cores associated with the Builder's created world. The group also accepts that Farrah cannot simply be restored after death. Sophie gains a powerful reflex ability. In a three-team mirage exercise, Jason's group manipulates Beth Cavendish's and Rick Geller's teams into fighting before ambushing both sides. The victory demonstrates strong planning and coordination, but the group still needs experience and further advancement before Emir's undisclosed challenge. Outside the team, Dorgan continues following the Builder operation's supply trail.

Emir announces that hundreds of Iron-rank entrants will compete for the legacy of the extinct Order of the Reaper. Before the contest, he and Jason stage a public break so Jason can serve as bait for the Builder cult. A Silver-rank cultist and three Bronze-rankers attack Jason and Sophie, but all four self-destruct before capture. Jason nevertheless obtains an intact starseed. He also recognizes that Landemere Vane, whom he previously killed, was a Builder cultist. Jason, Rufus, Clive, Emir, and Danielle begin to suspect that the Church of Purity helped the cult around the Vane estate. Anisa then uses Lamprey's authority to seize the intact starseed from the Magic Society for supposed destruction. Jason allows it, preserving the group's concealed advantage and giving them a possible way to watch the church. The Purity connection remains unproven, while Dorgan's shipping inquiry and Rufus's trusted investigation continue. The contest is now both a prize expedition and a possible front in the Builder conflict.

The competitors descend beneath Skyscar Lake and enter the City of Fallen Echoes, where the gate scatters Jason's team across separate towers. Jason and Sophie travel together through a city dense with monsters and magical rewards. The trial administrator explains that the ruined astral space belonged to the Order of the Reaper. The Churches of Purity and the Unliving destroyed the Order's presence there and released Vorgia, which transformed trapped initiates into adaptive flesh abominations. Entrants must pass trials of wisdom, capability, courage, intellect, and resolve before reaching the legacy. Jason and Sophie choose the wisdom reward, receiving escape medallions and rare emergency potions rather than immediately taking the dangerous courage test. They begin searching for the rest of their team while keeping those emergency resources in reserve.

Jason and Sophie find murdered entrants and then reconnect with Neil, Jory, and Imran Keen during an attack involving Vorgia. Their temporary group destroys a newly transformed flesh abomination by forcing it to adapt between speed and durability while Jason's necrotic afflictions accumulate. Elsewhere, Clive joins Valdis and wins a paired set of legendary magical weapons, while Humphrey remains committed to rejoining his own friends. Dorgan uncovers secret shipping, huge bribes, and vanished investigators, and Rufus privately identifies the Church of Purity as the leading suspect. At the city center, Beth Cavendish organizes survivors against an enormous blood-root vine blocking access to the final tower. Jory identifies its vulnerable root network, and the assembled force digs toward it. Jason sends Colin into the roots and applies escalating afflictions, causing the vine to rot across the central district. Its tentacles and spawned creatures begin falling inert, allowing the route toward the center to reopen, although the vine's final state is not yet confirmed.

Survivors regroup around Fallen Echoes' central tower. Jason's whole team is alive, while Jory remains with them after his companions evacuate. The Reaper rewards include unique awakening stones, and Jason and Humphrey accept the lethal courage trial. Humphrey rejects a vision of failing to protect his family. Jason confronts a tyrannical possible version of himself and refuses that path. He solves the intellect trial and then refuses an order to execute ancient prisoners, discovering that independent judgment is the real test of resolve. In Greenstone, Thalia proves the returned Thadwick is a projected double, destroys two compromised guards, and learns that the cult has abducted her son again while preparing an astral attack on Greenstone and the Delta. Jason then deduces that the Order's extinction is a cover for a continuing covert network. He passes its hidden trial, receives the genuine Scythe of the Reaper and a token, and exits with his team. Their shared quest reward evolves all five members' racial gifts.

Back with Emir, the team tests its evolved gifts and limits knowledge of Jason's role in triggering them. Jason receives the contest's awakening stones and bonds the Cloud Palace growth reward. Combining a Reaper token with an awakening stone gives him a Shadow of the Reaper familiar ability, while further stones complete his dark and doom sets with a shadow arm and another familiar. Neil and Humphrey also complete important parts of their power sets. Several gods publicly thank Jason for freeing the people trapped in Fallen Echoes. Their concentrated attention injures and refines his aura, granting the title Godless Prophet and leaving a detectable transcendent trace. Sophie completes a flexible set focused on movement, brief invulnerability, redirection, and fighting more effectively under pressure. Belinda begins taking her own essences, gaining storage, conjured tools, teleportation, and curse abilities. Clive also reveals that Lamprey has effectively removed him from ordinary Magic Society work because of his association with Jason.

Belinda absorbs the Charlatan confluence and reaches Iron rank, gaining shapeshifting and aura-masking abilities. At the same time, Cole begins arranging for a Silver-rank adventurer to abduct Jason, with Sophie as another target. Hester takes the team to Jayapura to sell its trial loot and buy rare materials. Jason receives an Immortal Crest, while the group studies professional arena teams and recognizes major gaps in its experience. Hester also warns that another Reaper finalist and every companion who travelled with that person have vanished without possessions or trace. Jason summons Shade, the former trial administrator, as a familiar, adds the combat familiar Gordon beside Colin, and helps Belinda summon Shimmer and Gemini. Returning to Greenstone, Jason bonds Emir's final reward, a soulbound Cloudflask, and configures it as a three-story houseboat. Sophie, Belinda, Clive, Humphrey, and Neil move in with him so the six-person team can train as a single unit.

Jason's team begins intensive training in the Cloudflask houseboat, integrating new familiars and abilities while planning Mirage Arena contests to test its coordination. Valdis remains in Greenstone to train with Rufus. Dorgan's shipping inquiry identifies a cult island after Mercer pressure forces the enemy to move supplies. A mixed-rank strike force attacks and confirms Church of Purity priests, Builder cultists, constructs, portal devices, and a Gold-rank priest. Arella leads the assault on constructs while Constance leads the lower-rank sweep. Unexpected Silver-rank cultists force Constance's element to retreat, and Rufus intervenes. He recognizes a powerful abomination as Farrah's killer and refuses to withdraw. Rufus builds a large field of sun and moon effects and unleashes Kingdom of Eclipse, killing many enemies and grievously wounding the killer. The abomination survives. Rufus collapses exhausted and surrounded as it approaches him. The cult is escaping through its portal network with Thadwick still alive in its custody, and Rufus's immediate fate remains unresolved.
