description.text: He Who Fights with Monsters 3 continues Jason Asano's story as Greenstone works through the aftermath of a cult raid and prepares for the next stage of conflict. While training his team against rival adventurers and pursuing new knowledge that could eventually help him return to his own world, Jason also faces political consequences from his methods and a personal injury that leaves him permanently marked. When old enemies orchestrate his abduction and attempt to force a dangerous magical parasite into his body, Jason must resist the ritual from within captivity while his allies race to find him before it is too late.

recaps.ending:
Clive completes the central tower inversion, destroying the World Engineers' deployment route and opening a portal home. Jason holds off the Builder long enough for the plan to succeed, then dies after carrying the Builder's vessel out of the tower. His body dissolves, and the World Phoenix token sends his soul onward under a pact that permits a return but forbids any later resurrection. Jason's friends do not learn that return is possible and mourn him as dead.

Thadwick Mercer is gone. A separate energy vampire rises from his abandoned body, takes fragments of his memories, consumes the soul imprisoned with the sealed sword, and escapes. The Adventure Society claims the astral space as a temporary base. Clive and Belinda take Magic Society and Builder-related work, while Sophie, Humphrey, and Neil travel with Emir on a Reaper investigation. Jory expands low-cost alchemical training through the Church of the Healer. On Earth, Jason remains officially dead and the investigation into his disappearance is suppressed. The Builder is formally barred from new vessels, starseeds, and tokens in the affected world, but its broader interworld scheme remains active. Dawn reveals that its magical siphon is delaying the monster surge in preparation for a catastrophic backlash threatening both linked worlds.
recaps.in_short: Jason Asano's team trains toward bronze rank while the Builder Cult prepares to reclaim a sealed astral space. After surviving Cole Silva's attempt to implant a starseed, Jason helps reopen the space and enters it with Humphrey, Clive, Sophie, Belinda, and Neil. They discover dormant World Engineers and an invasion force led by the Builder through mortal vessels. Clive devises a way to invert the central tower, destroy the deployment system, and reopen the exit. Sophie kills Zato, while Jason tackles the Builder from the tower so Clive can finish the inversion. Jason dies in the fall, but a World Phoenix token carries his soul onward. His friends return, recover the astral space, and mourn him without knowing he may come back. A new energy vampire escapes in Thadwick Mercer's body, and the surviving team separates for Builder and Reaper investigations. The final disclosure links Jason's two worlds and reveals that the Builder is engineering a magical backlash that could endanger both.

recaps.text:
Previously: Jason Asano, an outworlder in Greenstone, became an adventurer and formed a team with Humphrey Geller, Clive Standish, Sophie Wexler, Belinda, and Neil Davone. Rufus Remore, Gary, and Farrah helped guide him, but Farrah was killed during the conflict with the Builder Cult. The cult also compromised Thadwick Mercer and operated through hidden agents and starseeds, while figures such as Cole Silva and Lucian Lamprey remained threats closer to home.

Jason's group survived the Reaper Trials in a sealed astral space connected to the Order of the Reaper. The aftermath left dead adventurers, trapped victims, and unresolved cult activity. Jason's unusual powers, his familiars Shade, Gordon, and Colin, and recovered work associated with Landemere Vane all became relevant to the wider struggle. As this volume begins, Greenstone is recovering from the cult's island raid, the Church of Purity faces investigation for cooperation with the cult, and Jason still hopes to find a way back to his original world.

Jason receives dimensional research supplied through the Goddess of Knowledge. Clive combines it with Landemere Vane's work and concludes that travel between worlds may be a practical research goal. Jason's Adventure Society reassessment does not immediately restore his standing, so he accepts a supervised road contract to prove his discipline and give his team field experience.

Before leaving, the team finally defeats Valdis's group in a Mirage Chamber match by exploiting its protective response to the prince and combining Clive, Belinda, Neil, and Jason's abilities. Henrietta Geller then joins as the road party's bronze-rank supervisor. A silver-rank manifestation in Greenstone produces water elementals, confirming that dangerous manifestations are increasing even if the full monster surge has not begun.

The local Builder Cult has not been eliminated. Zato and Timos are secretly constructing an astral bridge from the former Vane estate to the sealed space. They expect reclaiming it to destroy Greenstone and a vast surrounding area, making the hidden operation an immediate regional threat.

Henrietta subjects the team to difficult field exercises designed to replace rigid plans with trust and improvisation. Jason and Belinda develop an effective affliction combination, while Neil, Clive, Humphrey, and Sophie learn to operate in unfamiliar groupings. At the ruined Vane estate, the party fails to detect Zato and Timos's concealed base.

A silver-rank Oasis Tyrant manifests beside a quarry village. Jason stays behind alone to draw it away from the evacuation, losing Shade's bodies and Gordon's vessel before being struck unconscious. Henrietta kills the monster after most villagers escape. Jason survives with a permanent soul scar, receives new protection and suppression resistance, and begins advancing individual abilities to bronze rank.

Back in Greenstone, Cole Silva exploits the disorder in the criminal underworld. He joins Killian Laurent and Lucian Lamprey in a plan to abduct Jason without leaving useful magical evidence. During a gathering at Cloud Palace, Jason's companions receive notice that his powers have been suppressed and their party has been forcibly disbanded. They do not know where he has been taken.

Cole Silva and Killian Laurent hold Jason at an abandoned outpost and implant an intact Builder starseed. The seed can only gain his soul if he yields, so it subjects him to escalating pain while Colin fights its physical effects. Jason refuses the Builder and exhausts the ritual's power. Colin purges the dead fragments and becomes dormant, leaving Jason gravely injured but spiritually unconquered.

Killian reveals that he has been using Cole, steals resources, and escapes. Jason forces his aura through the suppression collar, frees himself, and turns the restraints on Cole before Danielle Geller brings his allies to the outpost. Recovery is difficult, and his changed relationship with his soul gives him unusually strong aura and suppression abilities.

Carlos Quilido, a gold-rank healer specializing in starseeds, examines Jason. Public rituals confirm that the Builder scarred but never breached his soul. Lucian is captured while trying to flee Greenstone, while Killian remains at large. Elspeth Arella restores Jason's three-star standing and provides help replacing his familiars. Jason also reveals that his developing shadow portal may offer a route back into the sealed Reaper astral space.

Jason resummons Shade and Gordon and brings Colin back in a stronger bronze-rank form, though invasive magic still triggers memories of the starseed ordeal. He resumes contracts and training, suppresses violence in Old City by supporting formal authority for Adris Dorgan, and completes a lethal mission against slavers in the Veldt. The ease with which he executes them troubles him.

Research at Sky-Scar Lake confirms that Jason and Clive can reopen the sealed astral space. Sophie becomes free when her indenture ends and chooses to remain with the team. Jason detects a hidden starseed carrier, giving Greenstone's anti-cult council a way to screen important figures. The Adventure Society authorizes the six-person team to enter alone, expecting cultists, trapped flesh abominations, and no certain way home. Cole and Lucian are sentenced to permanent suppression, while Jory chooses healing and low-cost alchemy over renewed adventuring.

Jason's portal finally activates. Jason, Humphrey, Clive, Sophie, Belinda, Neil, and Stash cross together into the Order of the Reaper's altered astral space.

The team arrives on an outer tower and discovers that magical density has risen enough to strengthen monsters and interfere with the return portal. Each of the twelve outer towers contains a dormant diamond-rank construct called a World Engineer. The party does not yet know who built the city or what the constructs are meant to do.

Tracking evidence suggests that the missing cultists have reached bronze rank or changed. At the center, the team finds a silver-rank Bloodweaver's nest and evidence that it captured the cult group. Unable to face the monster safely, the adventurers retreat, survive an ambush by its vampiric servants, and begin an intensive cycle of hunting and advancement. Clive and Humphrey reach bronze rank. Clive determines that magic is being forced into the astral space, accelerating its eventual collapse and preventing escape until the cause is stopped.

Outside, Zato's operation has already fixed the astral tunnel on its destination. He invokes a pact requiring Nicholas Hendren, Anisa Lasalle, and their Purity force to enter when it opens. The bridge is expected within months.

The party undertakes dangerous battles to reach bronze rank before challenging the Bloodweaver. In an underground prison they defeat waves of constructs and altered creatures, then discover a black-and-red sword sealed with a powerful disembodied soul. Clive's brief contact confirms that the weapon must remain imprisoned. Neil and Jason reach bronze rank, joining Clive and Humphrey, and Jason restores Shade and Gordon in stronger forms.

At the Vane estate, Zato secretly subjects Thadwick Mercer and Dougall to a Builder process that depends on their willingness. In the astral space, rising magic becomes increasingly urgent. Jason's team enters the Bloodweaver's territory, accepts a mass ambush, and establishes a defensive platform. Jason fights among the vampiric horde while the others combine Clive's rituals, Belinda's control, Neil's protection, Humphrey's summons, Sophie's speed, and their familiars.

After a prolonged siege, Neil withdraws the team into a dimensional refuge, restores their mana, and unleashes an attack that breaks the remaining horde. Eight human figures then emerge from the jungle, bringing the suspected cultists into direct view.

The eight missing cultists have become the Bloodweaver's vampire minions and are killed. The Bloodweaver itself has fled. Dougall then reaches silver rank and immediately loses control of his body to the Builder, who orders preparations for the World Engineers and demands Jason alive. The team finds the cult's beacon and learns that the dimensional breach is close to opening. Belinda reaches bronze rank, and the party later kills the relocated Bloodweaver.

The ring gate activates, bringing the Builder Cult and its Purity allies into the astral space. The Builder raises a fortress through Dougall's deteriorating body. Nicholas Hendren agrees to sacrifice lower-ranked followers so selected Purity personnel can be converted to bronze. Jason scouts through Shade, refuses to rescue the captive Thadwick, and rejects Zato's offer to abandon the space in exchange for passage home.

The team ambushes an enemy force. Humphrey kills Anisa, Timos escapes under Jason's tracking mark, and Hendren nearly destroys the group. Humphrey survives a fatal blow through Immortality. Sophie wounds Hendren, Belinda steals his cleansing spell, and Jason converts accumulated sin into effects Hendren cannot remove before executing him.

After Hendren and Anisa die, the Builder converts captured Purity clergy into blank-minded, regenerative soldiers. It abandons Dougall's ruined body, takes Thadwick Mercer as its next vessel, and sends the former vessel out as an energy ghoul. Jason's team intercepts and destroys the ghoul before it can reach the soul imprisoned with the sealed sword.

The Builder uses probing attacks to study the team and raises a central tower where the Reaper trial tower once stood. At an outer tower, Jason steals a technical notebook that appears to explain sabotage. Clive recognizes it as genuine information arranged as a trap. The team pretends to follow the false plan while he investigates the system.

Clive discovers that the astral space is an artificial vessel built to deliver its dormant World Engineers to other worlds. The Order of the Reaper had repurposed their power for portals, and the Builder is restoring the original deployment function. Clive devises an inversion that can destroy the World Engineers and release enough power to open a way home. To perform it, the team must carry his calibration device through the Builder-held central tower.

Jason and Sophie drive a monster herd into the Builder's fortified camp while Belinda breaches the gate. Humphrey ambushes Zato, and Jason draws the Builder away so the rest of the team can reach the tower. The Builder, occupying Thadwick's body, is immune to Jason's afflictions. Zato reveals a self-repairing metallic form and repeatedly restores himself, leaving the team near defeat.

Sophie develops Boundary Breaker, Humphrey evolves a costly sacrificial attack, and Belinda steals Zato's renewal ability. Under Neil's enhancement, Sophie strikes with overwhelming resonating force and destroys Zato. Clive carries his ritual device upward while continuously adjusting the inversion.

Jason evades the Builder until a suppression collar traps him and severs the party interface. He briefly forces his way through the suppression, uses a gold spirit coin, and tackles the Builder out of the tower. The delay lets Clive complete the inversion, stopping the World Engineers from entering their world and restoring an exit. Jason dies in the fall. His equipment returns to storage, and the World Phoenix token is consumed.

The surviving team returns through the portal and immediately summons a rescue force. The Builder abandons Thadwick's failing body when Jason's World Phoenix token activates. A new creature rises from that body, consumes the soul that had guarded the sealed sword, and escapes with fragments of Thadwick's memories. The rescue party finds Jason's impaled body, but it dissolves into rainbow smoke. His friends believe him dead.

The Builder seeks to prevent Jason's return, but the World Phoenix token protects his passage. A settlement among great astral beings bars the Builder from placing new vessels, starseeds, or tokens in the affected world. Jason may return under the agreement, but afterward no power may resurrect him again.

The escaped energy vampire tells Thalia Mercer that Thadwick is gone and overpowers her. The Adventure Society takes control of the astral space as a temporary exploration base. Gabrielle tells Clive that Jason's soul was safely sent onward, but she withholds the possibility of his return. Clive is recruited for Builder-related work, while Emir directs Sophie and Humphrey toward an investigation involving the Order of the Reaper.

In the aftermath, Sophie is offered a guardian-like responsibility for Emilia's granddaughter. On Earth, authorities conceal the impossible disappearance of Jason's Melbourne apartment. Erika Asano receives evidence from the former detective who pursued the case, but withdraws for her family's safety. The detective is approached by rival secret organizations, leaving the Earth investigation unresolved.

The accessible astral space becomes a temporary research and training site while it moves away from the world. Jason's grieving friends prepare to separate: Clive and Belinda take Magic Society work, while Sophie, Humphrey, and Neil travel with Emir. Jory expands his low-cost alchemical methods through the Church of the Healer.

Dawn, First Servant of the Cult of the World Phoenix, reveals the larger conflict. Jason's magical world and Earth are patterned counterparts altered by a previous Builder. The current Builder linked them and is siphoning magic into Earth, which explains the halted monster surge. It intends the accumulated magic to rebound in a far greater flood, weaken the dimensional barrier, and threaten both worlds. The World Phoenix regards Jason as its most promising indirect agent against that plan.
